summary:
MicroFire is an interactive scientific observatory and immersive educational platform that transforms NASA's microgravity combustion research into accessible, evidence-driven experiences.

Developed for the Flame in Freefall challenge, MicroFire combines an interactive research dashboard, transparent evidence ranking, source-linked scientific explanations, an illustrative Flame Lab, and five distinctive 3D missions. Users can investigate combustion conditions, explore verified NASA observations, evaluate scientific claims, and examine hypothetical lunar habitat scenarios.

Our approach prioritizes scientific integrity: every supported conclusion is traceable to its source, missing measurements remain unknown, and unsupported safety conclusions are explicitly refused. A Research Passport documents users' scientific decisions and supporting evidence.

By connecting scientific research with interactive learning, MicroFire aims to make space combustion research more accessible to students, educators, and researchers worldwide, while encouraging better-informed investigations into fire behavior and future human space exploration.

We believe the future of space safety begins with understanding the evidence, not guessing beyond it.
details:
MicroFire — Evidence First. Explore Beyond.

The Problem

Fire behaves differently in microgravity. Without buoyancy, gravity, oxygen, airflow, pressure and material properties shape a flame in ways that Earth tests can miss, and that matters for every spacecraft, space station, lunar base and Mars habitat where people will live.

NASA has conducted many combustion investigations, but comparing their findings, and knowing what they do and do not prove, is difficult for students, educators and even researchers outside the field.

Our Solution

MicroFire is a web-based scientific observatory that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA microgravity combustion research, and turns it into interactive experiences people can play, compare and trust.

Instead of static reports, users investigate real observations, compare conditions fairly, test claims against evidence, and see exactly where the evidence stops. Every supported conclusion links to its NASA source, missing values stay unknown, and unsupported safety conclusions are refused.

How MicroFire Answers the Challenge

  • Summarizes: NASA investigations are described from NASA's own pages, with source links.
  • Ranks: investigations are ranked for five crew environments, with every point explained.
  • Interprets: an evidence engine states what a NASA record supports, what it does not, and why.
  • Relevance: spacecraft cabins, space stations, lunar and Martian bases, pressurized rovers, and fire-safety spinoffs on Earth.

Core Features

1. Scientific Evidence Workstation

An interactive scientific dashboard that enables users to:

  • Ask research questions about microgravity combustion.
  • Retrieve and rank relevant, admitted NASA evidence.
  • Compare recorded and hypothetical conditions.
  • Trace every claim to its original source.
  • Identify missing measurements and unsupported conclusions.
  • Explore the limits of transferring a result to another environment.

The evidence engine is deterministic: transparent ranking, citation verification, condition matching and explicit abstention rules.

2. Verified Experiment Record (BASS-II Test B20)

Our admitted record, BASS-II test B20, was checked cell by cell against NASA's original technical report. This review identified a discrepancy between uncalibrated and calibrated oxygen readings.

MicroFire keeps the correct calibrated value of 17.4 vol% oxygen and links it directly to NASA Technical Memorandum TM-20210011385, Table A.1, PDF page 112.

One experiment is admitted to the verified catalog today, while 55 legacy records remain quarantined until they pass source review.

3. Fire-Safety Investigation Atlas

Fourteen NASA combustion investigations, including FM2 on the Moon, SoFIE, FLARE, BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, SAME, DAFT, FLEX, ACME, SLICE and SPICE, summarized from NASA's own pages and ranked for five crew environments: spacecraft cabin, space station, lunar base, Mars base and pressurized rover.

Every ranking point is explained, never hidden.

It also shows a coverage matrix across prevention, detection and suppression, the ISS facilities where these experiments burn, the history of fire in crewed spaceflight, and NASA fire-safety spinoffs on Earth.

4. Comparison Studio

A fair-test comparator: two flame scenarios side by side, with a verdict that states whether the comparison is controlled (one variable changed) or confounded (several changed).

It adds gravity and oxygen ladders, a three-way comparison of NASA investigations, NASA imagery at glovebox and spacecraft scale, and how close each scenario is to the admitted NASA record.

Record-to-record comparison is refused until a second record passes review. It is never invented.

5. Interactive Flame Lab

Users change gravity, oxygen and airflow, predict the flame, run the experiment in a 3D chamber, and compare the result with NASA's documented B20 observation.

The flame is explicitly identified as an educational model, not a validated combustion simulation or physical measurement.

6. 3D ISS Adventure

A first-person, microgravity space-station lab. Users float with inertia, read the real NASA BASS-II B20 record at a research terminal, collect and install the BASS-II apparatus, run test B20, and answer Mission Control.

The honest answer: one orbital test cannot certify a lunar habitat as fire-safe.

Playable with keyboard, mouse, touch joystick or a "Guide me" assist.

7. Five Immersive Scientific Missions

MicroFire turns scientific reasoning into an interactive learning journey through five distinctive environments:

  • Station Arrival — Discover and collect the NASA evidence.
  • BASS-II Training Bay — Assemble the apparatus, then diagnose and repair a fault.
  • Flame Detective — Prediction, observation and scientific interpretation.
  • Claim Trial — Classify scientific claims against the evidence.
  • Lunar Habitat — A hypothetical habitat, its evidence gaps, and a responsible decision.

Every step is checked on the server, and each mission adds a cited entry to the user's Research Passport, which records scientific decisions, verified progress, supporting evidence and limitations.

8. Guided and Accessible Experience

PIX, an on-screen guide, gives step-by-step help on every page, and Mission 02 highlights the next action to take.

The platform includes responsive mobile interfaces, keyboard-accessible controls, a lightweight 2D mode for limited bandwidth or devices without WebGL, and optional ambient music generated in the browser.

9. Responsible Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Research

Our team investigated whether machine learning could be applied to microgravity combustion data.

We evaluated logistic regression, decision trees, random forests and a no-feature baseline using legacy BASS and BASS-II records.

The best candidate, logistic regression, reached a balanced accuracy of only 0.50 under grouped cross-validation, no better than chance, and the data had unresolved calibration and provenance issues. We therefore deliberately excluded the model from the deployed decision pipeline and documented this decision on the platform.

MicroFire will not show a prediction it cannot defend.

10. Judge Proof Mode

A 60-second guided demonstration connects a documented NASA combustion observation to a hypothetical lunar habitat, shows which conditions differ, and explains why the available evidence cannot certify that habitat as fire-safe.

Technology and Architecture

MicroFire was developed using:

  • Next.js, React, TypeScript, HTML and CSS
  • Three.js for interactive 3D environments and scientific illustrations
  • glTF-Transform for 3D model optimization
  • Node.js for application services
  • PostgreSQL for persistent, server-authoritative gameplay
  • Zod for structured data validation
  • Deterministic evidence retrieval and scientific reasoning algorithms
  • Logistic regression, decision trees and random forests for the machine learning evaluation
  • Web Audio API for generated ambient music
  • Playwright and Vitest for automated testing
  • GitHub for version control and collaborative development
  • Vercel for cloud deployment
  • Meshy AI for selected illustrative 3D models, labelled in the platform and video
  • OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code for AI-assisted software engineering
  • whisper.cpp for caption timing in video production

Creativity and Innovation

MicroFire integrates real scientific evidence with immersive, decision-driven gameplay.

Instead of rewarding users for guessing, it rewards examining evidence, identifying uncertainty, testing claims, and recognizing when the available information is not enough.

Its evidence-aware architecture keeps NASA observations, interpretations, hypothetical scenarios and illustrative visualizations visibly separate.

Refusing an unsupported conclusion is a deliberate scientific design choice, not a missing feature.

Intended Global Impact

MicroFire makes NASA combustion research accessible to students, educators, researchers, engineers and space enthusiasts worldwide.

As more records pass independent review, MicroFire can support richer research comparisons, reveal knowledge gaps, and help shape better research questions for future crews on the Moon, Mars and beyond.

Our long-term vision is an accessible bridge between space science, interactive technology, responsible artificial intelligence and science education.

Scientific Responsibility

MicroFire is an independent educational and research-support project. It does not provide operational fire-safety certification, replace qualified scientific assessment, or imply NASA endorsement.

Every supported conclusion remains within the boundaries of its evidence.
